correctness.rationale: For Q=D^T(DD^T)^+D, a column is an electrical dipole current vector; its absolute sum gives the l1 norm, while P=I-Q has column norm 1+||Qe||_1-2R_e. The supplied 6-cell A0 and 9-cell A1 potential tables solve grounded Laplacian equations, and fixed difference signs yield A(m,n), U(m,n) and W,Z. Strict hub-layer dominance follows the two polynomial comparisons (for cut, the candidate bracket sum is (m-n)^2+2(m+n)+8>0; for cycle each candidate difference is positive). The exact hub differences factor 2(m-n)(mn-2m-2n)/Delta and 2(m-n)(mn-4m-4n-2)/Delta. The positive deficits from 5 and 6 show finite nonattainment and m=r,n=r^2 give limits. Independent full-graph rational grounded-Laplacian solves checked all four orbit classes for (m,n)=(2,2),(2,3),(3,2),(3,3),(3,4), not using the proof voltage tables.
residual_risks: Only five small integer pairs independently computed; unbounded conclusion depends on hand-checked rational identities and inequalities.

originality.rationale: Best-of-knowledge PASS. Primary Dilworth–Kutzarova–Ostrovskii (arXiv:2305.12582) develops graph cycle-space projections, invariant/minimal projection framework and Hamming graph/cube families, but those use complete-graph factors, whereas K_{1,m} with m>=2 is noncomplete and has four distinct edge orbits. Their general projection machinery does not state these two rational columns or opposite optimizing phase curves. Same-area cactus basis-projection results have a different operator and graph class. A less-indexed electrical-network calculation could cover a special case.
residual_risks: Unindexed electrical network, resistance-distance or transfer-current literature may already have exact two-star absolute-current sums.
Exact per-parameter formulas corroborated on five pairs; mathematical universality rests on sign and polynomial claims.

value.rationale: Endpoint l1/l∞ norms of the canonical cut and cycle Hodge decomposition are intrinsic numerical graph invariants; their exact values over a natural two-parameter Cartesian family and explicit orbit maximizers are meaningful. Opposite maximizing edge directions for the two complementary operators persist for all (3,n),n>=7, with distinct sharp phase polynomials, unattained global constants 5 and 6, and different balanced vs strongly unbalanced limits. These are structural facts not a generic norm exercise or a table of small graphs.
residual_risks: No statement about arbitrary nonorthogonal projections or weighted stars.

limitations: Only unweighted Cartesian star products m,n>=2, real endpoint norms of canonical Euclidean-orthogonal projections.
